_doc: Source for scripts/build_paste_bundles.py. Each bundle is one round: a self-contained PowerShell text the PFM copies from its raw page and pastes into Windows PowerShell ISE (F5). It writes the files, then opens RADE, the Redacted Application Deployment Engine (a window; text prompts if no window can open): steps run one by one with a live log and PASS/FAIL counts, then one results folder (Rounds\\<round>: a report file plus copies of the PDFs, to attach to one e-mail; zips do not cross the boundary) and a summary for the clipboard. It runs only the steps inside it (PFM 3A). A step's "default" may be {passed, paths}: the step is ticked only when those files changed since the round that passed it; after a round passes it, set passed to the new hash (PFM 14 Nov 26). Never hand-edit scripts/gov/paste/*.ps1: change this file or the sources and rebuild. A step may list "needs" (check ids in the engine's $checkDefs) and "estimate" (minutes, used until a real run time exists). "apps" is the embedded catalog the Choose screen lists (name, plain-English summary, step names); without it, one application has every step. A guide step may set "doneText" (its Done button) and "doneLog" (the log line on Done).

bundles.title: Round R18: solution import test A r4 (lowercase workflow GUID; R17 A and B both failed: workflow not declared as a root component), a working solution export as the fallback, site setup r9 collects the A result; step bar fills left to right; It failed button

steps.name: T17 Solution import test A r4
steps.note: You import test solution A r4 and run its flow (about 5 minutes, an estimate). In R17 A and B failed: the flow was "not declared as a root component". r4 writes the flow ID in lowercase, as real exports do.
steps.url_source: Microsoft Learn, Power Automate US Government (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/us-govt): DoD maker portal; editable in the window, remembered in Config (agent value, PFM to confirm in R13)
guide: 1. Select Open in browser. Power Automate opens; sign in with your CAC if asked.
2. If the solution "90-161.Z solution import test A" or "... test B" is in Solutions from R17, leave it: the import replaces A.
3. Select Solutions (under More if you do not see it), then Import solution > Browse.
4. In the File name box press Ctrl+V (the file path is on the clipboard), select Open, then Next.
5. Connections: for SharePoint pick your existing connection. Select Import.
6. Wait for "Successfully imported" (1-3 minutes, an estimate). Open the solution "90-161.Z solution import test A",
open the flow "90161Z T17 Solution Import Test A r4", select Run, paste the new site address into "Site address", then Run flow.
7. Come back here and select "Done: the run has started".
If the import fails: copy the error message (no names or site address) into the box below, select It failed, then do the next step (the export).

steps.name: T17 Export a working solution (only if A failed)
steps.note: Only if test A failed: you export one solution that holds a working flow (about 5 minutes, an estimate), so the next build copies the real file layout. If A imported, select Skip.
steps.url_source: Microsoft Learn, Power Automate US Government (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/us-govt): DoD maker portal; editable in the window, remembered in Config (agent value, PFM to confirm in R13)
steps.doneLog: Confirmed by you: the export 90161ZExportSample is saved.
guide: If test A imported, select Skip this step.
1. In Power Automate select Solutions > New solution. Display name: 90161ZExportSample. Publisher: 90-161.Z (PFM). Select Create.
2. In the new solution select Add existing > Automation > Cloud flow > Outside Dataverse, tick one flow that works (for example the R13 probe flow), then Add.
3. Select Back to solutions (left arrow), tick 90161ZExportSample, select Export solution > Next.
4. Choose Unmanaged, select Export. Wait for the green bar, then select Download. The zip goes to Downloads: leave it there.
5. Come back here and select "Done: exported". The next step reads only solution.xml and customizations.xml from the zip, masks addresses, and collects them.
If the export fails: copy the error message (no names or site address) into the box below and select It failed.

steps.name: T17 Export reader r1
steps.note: Reads the export zip from Downloads (if there is one) and copies only solution.xml and customizations.xml to T17, addresses masked. No zip: one SKIP line.

steps.name: T16 Site setup r9
steps.note: Asks for the site address and a CAC sign-in, checks the site settings and the header logo (read-only), and collects the result of test A (waits up to 15 minutes).
